resolved.question: How many Democrats voted yea on Senate vote 257 (Axios: 21 plus King; Common Dreams: 22)?
resolved.answer: 21 Democrats voted yea, plus independent Angus King (Maine), for 73 yeas in total. Axios is correct. Common Dreams' 22 matches counting King, who is an independent, with the Democrats; the Washington Post editorial also says 22 members of the Democratic caucus. Roll call 257 party tally: D 21 yea / 23 nay / 1 not voting (Murphy); R 51 yea / 1 nay (Rounds) / 1 not voting (Sheehy); I King yea, Sanders nay.

resolved.question: Was the 73-25 vote on Nov. 9 or Nov. 10?
resolved.answer: Nov. 9, 2026 (vote 257, 5:31 p.m.): cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, 73-25. The vote on Nov. 10 was a different one: vote 258, 7:37 p.m., the motion to proceed itself, agreed to 62-21 with 17 senators not voting. Neither was passage of the bill.

evidence.quote: Senate Daily Press, Monday, Nov. 9: cloture invoked 73-25 at about 5:30 p.m.

resolved.question: What is H.R. 2347's official title, and why did the Senate Press Gallery call it the 'Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act'?
resolved.answer: H.R. 2347 is a House bill sponsored by Rep. Smucker, with the official title 'To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any damages, other than punitive damages, received on account of any sexual acts or sexual contact.' Its short title is the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act. Dates in the govinfo bill status: introduced 2025-03-25; reported by Ways and Means 2026-04-09 (H. Rept. 119-599); passed the House by voice vote 2026-04-27; received in the Senate 2026-04-28; placed on Senate Calendar No. 453 on 2026-07-14. The Press Gallery's Nov. 9 Daily Press entry used that short title because it is the bill's own name; the Senate is using this already-passed House bill as the legislative vehicle, and BAAJA (S. 5653) is offered as the Capito substitute SA 6883 to it. Later Daily Press entries describe it as 'legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill'. The Upriser article says the substitute keeps the House tax bill as a separate division; that was not checked against the amendment text, which congress.gov blocked.

evidence.quote: BILLSTATUS XML for H.R. 2347 (update date 2026-11-14; latest action 2026-11-11)
Daily Press entry for Nov. 9 using the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act name
Capito substitute amendment #6883 to H.R.2347, legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill.

resolved.question: Exact floor status through Nov. 15
resolved.answer: Nov. 10: after the 62-21 vote on the motion to proceed (vote 258), Sen. Thune moved to commit H.R. 2347 to the Finance Committee with instructions to report back forthwith with SA 6888; SA 6883 (Capito substitute, in the nature of a substitute) was proposed by Thune for Capito, and SA 6884 through SA 6890 were proposed by Thune, several nested on others (6884, 6886, 6888, 6889). Nov. 11, 12:29 p.m.: Thune filed cloture on SA 6883 and on H.R. 2347 (he also filed cloture on four district-judge nominations: Bennett, Coker, Reardon and Ballou). Per the Nov. 12 Daily Press, the cloture motions ripen at 5:30 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16; the Senate adjourned until 3:00 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, and the 5:30 p.m. votes are confirmation of the Domenico nomination, then cloture on the Capito substitute SA 6883 (the bill's own cloture vote follows). H.Con.Res.93 is set no later than Friday, Nov. 20. The Senate floor-activity pages for Nov. 13 and Nov. 14 show no activity. 'Amendment numbers filed' is stated as 'proposed' because that is the Senate record's wording.

evidence.quote: Amendment SA 6883 proposed by Senator Thune for Senator Capito.
Senate Daily Press, Nov. 11: cloture filed at 12:29 p.m. on SA 6883 and H.R. 2347

At 5:30 p.m., the Senate will proceed to a series of two votes: Confirmation of the Domenico nomination. Cloture on the Capito substitute amendment #6883 to H.R.2347, legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill.

resolved.caveat: congress.gov was blocked (403), so the Senate's own floor pages and Daily Press were used; the Nov. 15 status is the latest record found (nothing posted for Nov. 13-14, and Nov. 15 is a Sunday).

items.author: Chuck Schumer
items.title: Leader Schumer Statement After Permitting Reform Bill Advances In The Senate
items.summary: Schumer said he is voting to move the debate forward despite outstanding concerns with parts of the bill that he will seek to address through amendments. He credited Sens. Whitehouse and Heinrich.

quote.text: While I have outstanding concerns with parts of the bill that I’ll fight to address through the amendment process, I’m voting today to move this debate forward.
quote.speaker: Chuck Schumer, Democratic Leader, U.S. Senate

items.outlet: Office of Sen. Edward J. Markey
items.author: Edward J. Markey
items.title: Senator Markey Statement on Permitting Reform Deal
items.summary: Markey said he will vote against the motion to invoke cloture, citing timing, transparency, and threats to clean air, water and Tribes.

items.author: Jeff Merkley

items.title: Kaine Statement on Permitting Reform Legislation

quote.speaker: Tim Kaine, U.S. Senator (D-Va.)

items.outlet: Office of Sen. Chris Van Hollen
items.author: Chris Van Hollen
items.title: Van Hollen Statement on Current Opposition to Moving Forward with Permitting Reform Legislation

sources.quote: Vote Date: November 9, 2026, 05:31 PM Required For Majority: 3/5 Vote Result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to

events.title: Senate adopted the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347
events.summary: The Senate agreed, 62 to 21, to the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347 (roll call vote 258). Seventeen senators did not vote. The Senate floor record shows the measure laid before the Senate by motion the same day.

sources.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
sources.quote: By a vote of 62-21, the Senate adopted the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the vehicle for the permitting reform bill.

sources.title: Roll Call Vote 119th Congress - 2nd Session, Vote 258
sources.quote: Vote Date: November 10, 2026, 07:37 PM Required For Majority: 1/2 Vote Result: Motion to Proceed Agreed to

events.title: Thune proposed Capito substitute SA 6883 and amendments SA 6884 to SA 6890
events.summary: The Senate floor record for Nov. 10 shows Sen. Thune proposed SA 6883, in the nature of a substitute, for Sen. Capito, and proposed SA 6884 through SA 6890. It also shows a motion by Thune to commit H.R. 2347 to the Senate Finance Committee with instructions to report back forthwith with SA 6888.

sources.title: Senate Floor Activity - Tuesday, November 10, 2026
sources.quote: Thune to commit to Senate Committee on Finance with instructions to report back forthwith with the following amendment (SA 6888) made in Senate.

events.title: Thune filed cloture on SA 6883 and on H.R. 2347
events.summary: At 12:29 p.m. on Nov. 11 Sen. Thune filed cloture on the Capito substitute amendment SA 6883 and on H.R. 2347, per the Senate Daily Press.

sources.title: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
sources.quote: Senator Thune filed cloture filed cloture on the following: Capito substitute amendment #6883 to H.R.2347, Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.

events.title: Scheduled: 5:30 p.m. Nov. 16 votes include cloture on SA 6883
events.summary: Per the Nov. 12 Daily Press, the Senate stood adjourned until 3:00 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16, with two votes at 5:30 p.m.: confirmation of the Domenico nomination and cloture on SA 6883. The Senate floor activity pages for Nov. 13 and Nov. 14 show no further action.

sources.title: Thursday, November 12, 2026
sources.quote: At 5:30 p.m., the Senate will proceed to a series of two votes: Confirmation of the Domenico nomination. Cloture on the Capito substitute amendment #6883 to H.R.2347, legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill.

events.title: President Trump posts support for the bill (reported as a Sunday post)
events.summary: Per Bloomberg (published Nov. 9), President Trump's social media post on Sunday said the legislation would let pipelines, mines and power plants be built faster. The Nov. 8 date is inferred from 'Sunday' on the eve of the Nov. 9 vote; the article does not give the date.

sources.title: Trump says he backs energy permitting bill on eve of Senate vote
sources.quote: This Landmark Permitting Reform Legislation will codify our America First Energy Agenda, and ensure that we can build Pipelines, Mines, and Power Plants faster than ever before

events.title: OMB issues Statement of Administration Policy strongly supporting S. 5653
events.summary: OMB issued a Statement of Administration Policy dated Nov. 9 on S. 5653 that says the Administration strongly supports passage and that the President's advisors would recommend he sign it.

sources.title: S. 5653 - Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Statement of Administration Policy)
sources.quote: The Administration strongly supports passage of S. 5653, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.

events.title: Sponsors release a substitute amendment to H.R. 2347 / BAAJA
events.summary: The EPW and ENR committee leaders introduced a substitute amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, per MLex.

sources.title: US Senators introduce amendments to legislation on permit reform
sources.quote: Leadership of the US Senate Environment and Public Works Committee and Energy and Natural Resources committee introduced a subsitute amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026

sources.title: Senate permitting bill bolsters data center provisions, moves to full vote
sources.quote: The vote on cloture followed the November 7, 2026 release of the Manager’s Substitute Amendment, incorporating changes from negotiations with the House of Representatives, the Trump administration, Tribal nations

events.title: Trump says he will not approve wind turbines while backing the bill
events.summary: On Nov. 9 President Trump told reporters he was 100 percent behind the permitting bill and said he would not approve wind turbines.

sources.title: Trump Backs Energy Bill '100%' Before Balking at Wind Turbines
sources.quote: Trump added: “I know, but I won't approve it. Well, the bill hasn't been fully negotiated. I will not approve wind turbines because wind turbines are a major loser.”

sources.title: Senate Advances Permitting Overhaul But Roadblocks Loom
sources.quote: "I will not approve wind turbines because wind turbines are a major loser," he said during an impromptu news conference.

events.title: All Pueblo Council of Governors reiterates opposition after Senate vote
events.summary: The All Pueblo Council of Governors said on Tuesday it remains opposed to the bill after the Monday cloture vote.

sources.title: All Pueblo Council of Governors condemns US Senate vote advancing permitting reform bill
sources.quote: Nobody consulted the Pueblos before this bill was written, and the changes made since don’t fix that.

people.name: Chuck Schumer
people.position: Nov. 9: voted for cloture on the motion to proceed and said he has outstanding concerns he will try to address through amendments.

quote.text: While I have outstanding concerns with parts of the bill that I’ll fight to address through the amendment process, I’m voting today to move this debate forward.

people.name: Edward J. Markey
people.position: Nov. 9: said he will vote against the motion to invoke cloture, citing timing, transparency and threats to clean air, water and Tribes.

quote.text: Because of these issues on timing, transparency, and threats to our clean air, water, and Tribes, I will vote against the motion to invoke cloture on this legislation.

people.name: Jeff Merkley
people.position: Nov. 9: said transmission permitting reform is essential, said the bill accelerates the extraction and burning of fossil fuels, and said he would vote against the bill before the Senate.

quote.text: I will vote against the bill before us today, but I look forward to working with my colleagues to get permitting reform right.

people.name: Tim Kaine
people.position: Nov. 9: voted against the procedural motion over National Historic Preservation Act changes; said he could support the bill if his amendments succeed.

quote.text: For this reason, I am voting against today’s procedural motion. I will seek to amend the bill to address my concerns and, if successful, could support it with appropriate changes.

people.name: Chris Van Hollen
people.position: Nov. 9: voted against moving forward; said he cannot support the bill in its current form and is putting forward changes.

quote.text: I’m putting forward changes to the bill to address these concerns; however, while I support the goal behind tackling our burdensome and outdated permitting system, given this bill’s impact on Maryland, I cannot support it in its current form.

people.name: Michael Bennet
people.position: Nov. 9 vote: voted against advancing the bill; said it does not adequately protect Tribal cultural resources and should be vetted more thoroughly.

quote.text: These changes must be vetted more thoroughly before passing into law. Given these concerns, I cannot support advancing this bill at this time.

people.name: Alan Armstrong
people.position: Nov. 9 vote: called the 73-25 cloture vote a major step and urged the Senate to finish the bill.

quote.text: Tonight’s vote marks a major step forward. I applaud my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for coming together to advance meaningful permitting reforms

people.name: Mike Rounds
people.position: Nov. 9: the only Republican to vote against cloture; cited landowners' right to negotiate at state and local levels before federal intervention, in a Facebook post reported by SDPB.

quote.text: South Dakota landowners deserve to negotiate with stakeholders at the state and local level before federal intervention is required,

people.name: Mike Lee
people.role: U.S. Senator, sponsor of the substitute
people.position: Nov. 10 floor remarks: said it can take years to get permission to build a powerplant or transmission line, and that more energy is needed on the grid.

quote.text: Today, a company can spend years trying to get permission just to build a powerplant, and a transmission line

people.name: Tammy Duckworth
people.position: Nov. 9 vote: voted no; per The Washington Sun, concerned the package could hand Trump more power.

quote.text: Sen. Tammy Duckworth (D-Illinois) voted no, saying she was concerned the package could hand Trump more power.

people.name: Ben Ray Luján
people.position: Nov. 9 vote: voted no, citing concerns from tribal leaders, per The Washington Sun.

quote.text: Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-New Mexico) also voted against the bill, citing concerns from tribal leaders.

people.name: Catherine Cortez Masto
people.position: Voted yea on the Nov. 9 cloture motion; The Washington Sun, citing Punchbowl News, reported she said she would not support the bill unless provisions that affect tribal rights are removed.

quote.text: to say she would not support the bill unless provisions that affect tribal rights are removed

people.name: Brian Schatz
people.position: Nov. 9 vote: voted yes; said he would introduce amendments on Native Hawaiian and Tribal voice.

quote.text: Schatz said he would introduce amendments and continue working to "ensure Native Hawaiian organizations and Tribes have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their communities."

people.name: Fred Krupp
people.position: Nov. 9: said the latest version has important grid reforms but unwinds protections; wants improvements before final passage.

quote.text: The latest version has important reforms to get clean energy on the grid and upgrade our aging infrastructure, but it also unwinds protections for our air, water and communities,

people.name: Sheldon Whitehouse
people.position: At the Nov. 9 press conference, called the bill the floor, not the ceiling, of climate and environmental aspirations.

quote.text: "This bill is the floor, not the ceiling, of our climate and environmental aspirations," Whitehouse said at a press conference. "We look forward to working to accomplish big things with our big Democratic majorities."

people.name: Joey Sanchez
people.affiliation: All Pueblo Council of Governors (19 New Mexico Pueblos)
people.position: After the Nov. 9 vote, said the Senate advanced the bill without consulting the Pueblos and that the changes do not fix that.

quote.text: Nobody consulted the Pueblos before this bill was written, and the changes made since don’t fix that.

people.name: Rep. Nikki Budzinski
people.role: Representative (New Democratic Coalition vice-chair for policy)
people.position: At a Heatmap event on Tuesday, Nov. 10, said she disagreed with waiting until the next Congress to pass a permitting bill such as BAAJA and called the moment a very unique opportunity.

quote.text: "I'm done after the last two years of doing messaging bills on the floor. I think this is a very unique opportunity."
